n1.label: prevalence
n1.question: What is the mechanistic and technical distinction between constitutional (germline epimutation) vs. somatic BRCA1 promoter methylation? Which allele-specific bisulfite sequencing (AS-BSseq) protocols reliably distinguish them?
n1.search_query: constitutional BRCA1 promoter methylation germline epimutation allele-specific bisulfite sequencing somatic distinction
n1.execution_note: WebFetch denied. Grounded from dome memory and domain knowledge: Constitutional methylation = methylation present in all somatic tissues including blood/saliva (germline epimutation, often monoallelic). Somatic methylation = tumor-restricted, often biallelic, arises during oncogenesis. AS-BSseq distinguishes by comparing tumor vs. paired blood DNA methylation at BRCA1 CpG island. Key methodological papers: Hansmann et al. (AS-BSseq protocol); Flanagan et al. 2010 (germline BRCA1 epimutation in familial BC). Combined blood + tumor methylation profiling is the standard discriminator.

findings.summary: Constitutional methylation is detectable in blood/normal tissue; somatic is tumor-restricted. AS-BSseq comparing blood vs. tumor DNA is the validated discriminating protocol. Key gap: no standardized clinical-grade AS-BSseq assay approved for companion diagnostic use.

findings.note: Manual query required: 'constitutional BRCA1 methylation germline epimutation allele-specific bisulfite sequencing'.
